definitions.gloss: to soak in; to permeate; to seep into
definitions.explanation: for a liquid or substance to penetrate deeply into something

definitions.gloss: to sink in; to be deeply ingrained
definitions.explanation: for knowledge, habits, or feelings to become deeply established

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}が{地面|じめん}に{染|し}み{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: The rain soaked into the ground.

examples.japanese: たれが{肉|にく}に{染|し}み{込|こ}んでいる。
examples.english: The sauce has soaked into the meat.

examples.japanese: この{味|あじ}は{子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}から{体|からだ}に{染|し}み{込|こ}んでいる。
examples.english: This flavor has been ingrained in me since childhood.

examples.japanese: {疲|つか}れた{体|からだ}に{温|あたた}かい{風呂|ふろ}が{染|し}み{込|こ}む。
examples.english: A warm bath seeps into my tired body.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{習慣|しゅうかん}が{染|し}み{込|こ}んでいて、なかなか{変|か}えられない。
examples.english: Years of habit are so ingrained that it's hard to change.

examples.japanese: {出汁|だし}が{大根|だいこん}に{染|し}み{込|こ}むまで{煮|に}る。
examples.english: Simmer until the dashi soaks into the daikon.

examples.japanese: {親|おや}から{教|おそ}わった{礼儀|れいぎ}が{骨|ほね}の{髄|ずい}まで{染|し}み{込|こ}んでいる。
examples.english: The manners my parents taught me are ingrained to my very core.

notes:
{染|し}み{込|こ}む is a compound verb combining {染|し}みる (to stain, permeate) + {込|こ}む (into, deeply).

VERB TYPE:
- Godan verb ({込|こ}む conjugates as む-verb)
- Intransitive

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {水|みず}が{染|し}み{込|こ}む (water soaks in)
- {味|あじ}が{染|し}み{込|こ}む (flavor soaks in)
- {体|からだ}に{染|し}み{込|こ}む (to sink into one's body)
- {心|こころ}に{染|し}み{込|こ}む (to sink into one's heart)
- {骨|ほね}の{髄|ずい}まで{染|し}み{込|こ}む (to seep into one's very bones)

SENSE 1 VS SENSE 2:
- Sense 1: Physical penetration of liquids/substances
- Sense 2: Abstract/metaphorical - deeply learned or ingrained

COOKING USAGE:
- Very common in cooking instructions when describing how flavors penetrate ingredients
- Often used with {出汁|だし}, たれ, {煮汁|にじる}

RELATED WORDS:
- {浸透|しんとう}する (to permeate - more formal)
- {染|し}みる (to stain, seep - base verb)
- {吸|す}い{込|こ}む (to suck in, absorb)

REGISTER: Neutral. Common in everyday speech and cooking.
